name: Magnetic Map
goal_text: Measure the gases in the air above a big city for 12 weeks and send the readings to the ground.

requirements.reason: The spacecraft is heavier than the rocket slot allows.
requirements.tip: Remove a part or swap for a lighter one.
requirements.consequence: The launch provider refuses an overweight spacecraft, so you cannot launch.

requirements.text: Deliver at least 15 MB of air readings per week
requirements.reason: The radio sends less than the mission needs.
requirements.tip: A small radio is light but slow. Add a big antenna or a second ground station.
requirements.consequence: Fewer readings reach the ground each week.

requirements.reason: The parts use almost all the power the panels make.
requirements.tip: Use larger panels or a part that needs less power.
requirements.consequence: With no spare power, the battery drains a little every week.

requirements.text: Keep at least 10% of the budget in reserve
requirements.reason: There is too little money left for surprises.
requirements.tip: Choose cheaper parts or finish building sooner. Every day costs money.
requirements.consequence: A surprise cost in orbit can cancel the mission.

requirements.reason: The battery is too small to last through the dark part of the orbit.
requirements.tip: Add a battery or a larger one.
requirements.consequence: The satellite browns out in every eclipse and loses data. With no battery it dies.

requirements.reason: Building and testing took too long.
requirements.tip: Build faster. Each retest also adds days.
requirements.consequence: You miss your launch slot and pay to rebook a later one.

rocket.name: Big rideshare rocket
rocket.why: Dozens of small satellites share one big rocket, so a seat is cheap. You go where the big rocket goes, and your slot has a hard mass limit.

differences: Denmark's first satellite rode up as a secondary passenger on a Delta II and mapped Earth's magnetic field for many years.
